answers.answer: 1. “Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.” 2. “Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.” Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: quoted operative sentences.

answers.answer: 1. “Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM.” The acting player may peek at display blackmails. 2. “Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.” 3. “Finish the display step by discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card.” Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies; unused pensioners do not remain for another turn.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige and Retirements: quoted sentences.

answers.answer: 1. “Check where your opportunity marker was at phase start (it begins off the board).” 2. “Choose a main family action: take it once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched it.” 3. “Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.” 4. “After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.” “With at least four vacant offices, [Enlist Writer] place[s] one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.” Thus, with four offices vacant and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action places two writers plus the once-this-turn vacancy bonus, for three total.
answers.evidence: Family action steps and Enlist Writer row: quoted text; the three-writer result follows from those stated steps.

answers.answer: 1. “After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares.” 2. “With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order.” 3. “Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.” A share-seeker places a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pays the bank the price of that queue space (£2, £3, £3, £4 or £5); the applicant is not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family—Seek Share row and New Company shares paragraph: quoted operative sentences.

answers.answer: 1. “Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card.” 2. “When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order.” 3. “Own-family hiring needs verbal consent from every other player in that office's candidate pool,” with Chairman elections and Commander appointments exempt from Nepotism. 4. “If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.”
answers.evidence: Hiring and Nepotism: quoted sentences and exceptions table.

answers.answer: 1. “Former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins.” 2. “If no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder including self; no Nepotism consent.” 3. “Move one winner's Company shares into Chairman slot and give title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.”
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: quoted operative sentences.

answers.answer: 1. “First commit resources/cash: all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure, no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card into Vacant Offices.” Specific Commander/firm procedures modify this. 2. “You cannot take a dead action with no effect or chance of success: for example trade with no ship or deploy without dice to trigger possible officer losses.”
answers.evidence: Company Operation—Success checks: complete quoted procedure and restriction.

answers.answer: 1. “May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling majority Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end.” 2. “Then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. May interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting total borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Chairman: quoted borrowing/allocation procedure.

answers.answer: 1. “Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains.” 2. “Lease extra ship £2; fit ship from shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards.” 3. “Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Manager of Shipping: quoted sentences.

answers.answer: 1. “Declare regions for Trade: include home region, and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 President's treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. Failure can be retried during operations if affordable; catastrophe removes President. At most one successful Trade per President per turn.” 2. “Failed attempts and retries belong to that President's uninterrupted opportunity; another position cannot act between its attempts.” 3. “Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency's sea zone. Trade does not exhaust ships.” The first writer goes to home port; every later order must extend the connected route filled during this same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it. “Writers do not limit capacity: use all available writers, then continue filling with filled-order tokens for the remaining ships.” Those tokens continue this Trade's route. No President may fill another President's home region, even if its office vacant. 4. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation. President earns bank £1 per order; writer owners earn £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Actions—Presidency operations and Trade: quoted declaration, retry, capacity, route, limits, and payout rules.

answers.answer: 1. “Target own Presidency's home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. Cannot target another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. Company region must have unrest or a closed order to give action an effect.” 2. “Exhaust chosen officers/regiments to bottom for one die each and local alliances for printed dice. Subtract the combined strength of target and all other regions in its empire, counting target only once. Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll normal check; a noncatastrophic failure can retry using remaining resources.” 3. “After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in attempt; each 6 returns an officer to supply. Regiments never roll officer losses.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy, steps 1–3: quoted target, dice, penalty, retry, and loss procedure.

answers.answer: 1. “On success, take loot from the bank: £4 per target tower + faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of (surviving officers used in this attempt + 1).” Count only this attempt's surviving participating officers and used regiments/alliances. Pay each cycle: “Commander family first” gets £1 for the Commander plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; other families clockwise get £1 per used surviving officer; the bank last gets £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece, regardless of strength. “Repeat that entire cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed.” The Commander also receives one trophy per target tower. 2. After loot and trophies: remove the target tower and dome (and all matching empire flags throughout India if it was a capital); open all target orders and remove all its unrest; for a new conquest turn the loot/control token region-symbol side up above the associated President's box, put Governor overlay in the conquered region, and only the Governor card in Vacant Offices; if Elephant faced outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. Governor/overlay are not created with Governor General. 3. “On catastrophe, Commander returns half own family's trophies rounded up and Commander member to supply. Exhausted officers still check losses. Commander has no office card to vacate.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Deploy: successful loot/payout/control table and catastrophe paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. “Take the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result.” 2. “Success: Take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful; then choose exactly one option.” Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest in the region; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. On success choose one: a Build performs one stage (place a partial ship in the region if none exists; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor's President); commission a regiment into that President's associated Army; or Tax, adding an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury, with each Tax after the first this turn adding regional unrest. 3. “Repeat using the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remaining, or catastrophe.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Governors: Administer procedure, result and option tables; quoted operative text.

answers.answer: 1. Company expenses reduce Balance £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army and each ship in sea zones (including China), excluding Commanders. “If insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one only while a track space remains. At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt any further. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra current-turn expense. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower Standing two.” 2. “Expectations: Compare remaining Balance to the expectations under current Standing; if lower, lower Standing one.” 3. “Dividends: Chairman may pay any affordable number. Each dividend costs one cash per Company share; pay each owner £1 per share, including Chairman. If total cash paid as dividends is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.”
answers.evidence: Revenue—Company expenses, expectations and dividends: quoted sequence and rules.

answers.answer: 1. A normal Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve primary Crisis first, then secondary regions in Bombay → Madras → Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses the order of associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength is normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength plus unrest in its target region. Primary Foreign Invasion uses the ordinary attack die without added unrest. Each secondary Rebellion uses only the unrest cubes in that region, with no event modifier or empire strength. 2. Identify defender: if the associated Commander is occupied, that Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; if vacant, Military Affairs acts in the Commander's stead; if both are vacant, Chairman chooses. The acting player exhausts active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible. 3. “Newly exhausted pieces EQUAL Crisis strength: The attack FAILS; defense SUCCEEDS. Remove all unrest in the attacked region. The actual Commander gains one trophy; Military Affairs/Chairman substitutes gain OR lose NO trophies. If this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible.” (Substitutes do not gain or lose trophies.)
answers.evidence: Events—Attacks on Company, Mounting defense, and printed comparison table: quoted order, strengths, actors, and successful defense result.

answers.answer: 1. “−1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma's If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy.” 2. “Zero or higher passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy then immediate law effects.” Thus support 0 passes. 3. “Finally restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation, after either outcome.” If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Resolution: quoted pass/fail thresholds, failure PM/policy sequence, pass effect order and card restoration.

answers.answer: 1. In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting procedure and support threshold. 2. “No policy accompanies this vote, and PM may vote against it.” 3. On pass, lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM takes passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3 VP per share; PM stays in power and Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 begins deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: eligible scenarios/timing, pass/fail table and exceptions: quoted procedures.

answers.answer: 1. “Form a firm—only if you currently manage none: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. Flip your family board to its firm-charter side, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.” 2. To invest, with manager's consent make the same Company-share/workshop contribution to create one firm share and put £5 from the bank into London. There may be up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share; cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt are on a lined space; cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested, give no bonus or Company-failure VP, and remain invested even if firm fails. 3. “Investment cash always comes FROM THE BANK TO London. London cash cannot buy new equity shares; creating shares requires a Company-share or workshop contribution.”
answers.evidence: Deregulation treasury rules and Firms phase—Form/Invest bullets: quoted money sources, process and restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn; only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy, and it may select a closed home port. Managers select strategies simultaneously and secretly. For a trade zone/home port commit a secret cash bid from London; the selected home port must be open when filled, and selecting the strategy does not open it. Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends, but still pays expenses and retains the prior dividend marker for retirement. Reveal bids simultaneously, while strategy cards stay facedown until the matching Presidency begins. 2. At the start of that Presidency's operations, matching firms reveal and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1/2 permits trade. Firm initiative = ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative; successful President's Trade creates initiative the same way using Presidency ships. Fill lowest initiative first; President chooses among tied traders. If President vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governors have acted, with Chairman choosing ties. 3. Fill only open orders, up to ships + 1, starting at strategy home port and tracing that firm's own filled route back there. Each firm may fill a particular order only once this turn and cannot refill its own earlier order; it can refill an order filled by another firm or Company, and Company can refill firm orders. A previously filled order pays half listed revenue rounded down. Revenue goes to India treasury. Advance Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: quoted choice, reveal/check timing, initiative, capacity, repeat-fill restrictions/revenue and Value growth.

answers.answer: 1. At start of Revenue before Company, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm value; either or both firm treasuries may be used. 2. If unable, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to shipyards, charter to family side, and workshops remain invested. Emergency investment uses normal Company-share/workshop rules, even at the ten-share cap; it pays expenses, loses any remaining cash, and lowers Value one space per emergency investment. Alternatively, emergency merger with only one other firm uses normal merger procedure, including every involved shareholder's consent; the other firm must first pay its own expenses if needed, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses. 3. After expenses, manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. Waiving a dividend requires both the shareholder's choice and manager's consent. Record total actual cash paid out, not per-share dividend, as marker on Company Balance; active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero, while Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: quoted costs, dissolution/rescue, and payout rules.

answers.answer: 1. “Components are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible.” Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. “Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited.” 2. “All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.”
answers.evidence: Components—Limits: quoted supply, unlimited-track and information rules.

answers.answer: 1. May trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. May not trade officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. 2. “To transfer a share: return the old owner's family member and replace it at the share's location with a member from the RECEIVING FAMILY.” Blackmail may be shown privately but must stay facedown when traded; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Negotiation table and share-transfer paragraph: quoted tradable items and procedure.

answers.answer: 1. “Immediate transfer” agreements are binding. “Promise of future behavior” is nonbinding, except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect can be called if possible. 2. A promise card follows its own timing/limits, and no promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Promise cards may transfer to a third party or back to guarantor. 3. “Transferred resources cannot activate twice”: for example, a workshop that paid this Bonuses phase does not pay again after sale during that phase.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Agreement/promise table: quoted binding status, timing and exceptions.

answers.answer: 1. “Use that scenario's player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players. Shuffle and deal evenly.” 2. “Place every listed holding”: take listed cash from the bank and enterprise cards into the player's area; put each office's family member in its office and give the matching office card to its owner; put Company-share members in Court; put writers, officers and trainees in indicated Presidency/Army/Training boxes; put Commanders in their Army Commander slots without office cards; and put each matching ship in the listed sea zone or on its shipyard if unfitted. 3. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck; deal three for London Season display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4: quoted card count, holdings, luxury VP and display procedure.

answers.answer: 1. “The game ends after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring.” 2. “Once game over, stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.”
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions opening paragraph: quoted game-end and post-game rules.

answers.answer: 1. Count enterprises and Company shares using current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), plus 1 per passed-law token and trophy, 2 for PM, and printed card power, including faceup or facedown blackmail and applicable spouse. 2. Most/second awards are 3/1 VP for final turn 1–3, 5/2 for turn 4–6, and 8/4 for turn 7–8. “Tied first: only lower award to each tied player; no other award. Tied second receive none.” 3. Highest final VP wins; ties go to most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Power award and victory tie rule: quoted scoring sources, awards and tiebreakers.

answers.answer: 1. “If Company survived, add Court's current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.” 2. At final outcome, if survived, roll office attrition then retire Pensioners, with no prestige/display cards; if failed, draw one random Company failure card and resolve its printed consequence. 3. If deregulated, firm special scoring/retirement occur before ordinary scoring and the special retirement applies whether Company survived or failed; it is not replaced by the failure card.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Court/workshops, final retirements/failure table, and final scoring order: quoted outcome rules.

answers.answer: 1. “Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Make required enterprise/share trades immediately upon taking the spouse.” 2. “Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.” 3. Discounts reduce actual spending and therefore display priority.
answers.evidence: London Season—Spouses: quoted transfer restrictions, VP and discount timing.

answers.answer: “Whether a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; purchase becomes possible after the ship returns.”
answers.evidence: London Season—Returned shipyard rule: quoted sentence.

answers.answer: 1. Enlist Writer: place a member in any Presidency's Writers box; with at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn. Enlist Officer: place a member in Officers-in-Training. 2. Purchase Luxury: pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and its window icon; it is a social enterprise. 3. Purchase Shipyard: pay bank £2; take shipyard and put matching ship unfitted on it; it is a shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. 4. Purchase Workshop: pay bank £5; take workshop; it is manufacturing, has two votes and £1 bonus, and is worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. 5. Seek Share: place member on empty Stock Exchange space, pay bank the queue price (£2, £3, £3, £4, £5); it is an applicant, not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family action table: each purchase/enlistment row quoted with costs and immediate effects.

answers.answer: “If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too.” “If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.”
answers.evidence: Family phase: quoted piece-shortage and no-action rules.

answers.answer: “If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (lose prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.”
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: quoted empty-Court fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Director: Chairman chooses a current officeholder other than Chairman or Governor; if all offices are vacant, any writer. Commanders are not officeholders. Manager of Shipping: Chairman chooses any writer. 2. Military Affairs: Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander; if none, any officer; if none, any Officer-in-Training. 3. President: Director chooses a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. Governor: associated President chooses a writer or officer in the region; Commander is not an officer and is ineligible, and the member goes on the Governor overlay. 4. China Superintendent: Chairman chooses any writer, and office is hired immediately on creation. Governor General replaces Director of Trade and is hired the same way. Ordinary own-family hiring needs verbal consent from every other player in that office's candidate pool; Commander appointments and Chairman elections are exempt. If no candidate exists or hirer is vacant, skip office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring—office hirer/candidate table, Nepotism table and vacancy rule: quoted candidates and exceptions.

answers.answer: 1. “May make repeated Special Envoy checks: £1 treasury cash per die, no penalty.” Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing Superintendent overlay/card and having Chairman immediately hire a writer. 2. “After all envoys, may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones (including China once created). Cannot transfer while still taking envoys.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Director of Trade: quoted repeated checks, effect and transfer timing.

answers.answer: 1. “May make up to two transfers, each officer or regiment from one Army to another, remaining in top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army's top half.” 2. “Finally appoint Commanders: if vacancy or someone has more total family pieces in Army than current Commander's family, choose among families with most pieces. Move chosen officer to Commander slot; return previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with current Commander's family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Military Affairs: quoted operation order and replacement/tie rules.

answers.answer: 1. “Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade. Must allow each position an opportunity but Commander/Governors may decline. Each position finishes all actions before next begins. Trade can go before/after Commander or any Governor but cannot interrupt another position.” 2. “If President vacant, Chairman sets order only: cannot trade or approve local alliance purchases.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Presidency operations and Trade: quoted order, decline, interruption and vacancy rules.

answers.answer: “Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency's sea zone. Trade does not exhaust ships.” On Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency's Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep fatigue.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade and Upkeep/Refresh tables: quoted non-exhaustion and destinations.

answers.answer: 1. “At the START of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, first request President's treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in Army; President must approve purchase.” Move purchased alliances to top/active half. 2. “When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to the bottom half. Its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among more than one purpose.” 3. “Refresh exhausts any unused active alliances too; it does not reactivate alliances as it does officers/regiments.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy: quoted timing, funding, exhaustion, one-use and refresh rules.

answers.answer: “Deploying in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest: Company defense penalty is zero; no tower remains, so gain zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use the minimum loot of surviving participating officers + 1 for the Commander, distributing normally.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Deploying in an already Company-controlled region paragraph: full quoted rule.

answers.answer: 1. “Each successful Build performs one stage: if no partial ship is in the Governor's region, this single success places the partial ship there. If a partial ship is already there, this single success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor's President. Thus the two stages require two successes in total.” The partial ship has no other effect. 2. “Commission regiment: Place it in the Army associated with the Governor's President. Officer-like strength, loot paid to bank, no officer-loss rolls.”
answers.evidence: Actions—Governors: Administer option table: quoted Build stages and regiment treatment.

answers.answer: 1. China is created by a successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case the Chairman immediately hires any writer. 2. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director of Trade may send ships there like any sea zone. China ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: quoted creation, hiring, treasury and Eastern-zone rules; Company Operation says China acts after Bengal.

answers.answer: 1. China Trade can be attempted only once, including a failed attempt, with no retry; roll one die per ship. 2. Without an export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt China Trade. On success, count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Company Balance receives £4 times that number, and Superintendent's family receives £1 per icon from the bank. Non-Company export icons do not count; the Company payment is not a flat £4.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: quoted attempt limit, dice, eligibility, revenue and bonus table.

answers.answer: 1. “Law creates this office: immediately make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director of Trade with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue, and place its ribbon overlay.” 2. “No further Governors/overlays created upon conquest; printed Company symbols indicate controlled regions.” 3. Governor General uses former Director's treasury and turn position and is hired like Director; skip Governor Elimination when regions are lost.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governor General: quoted law transition and subsequent conquest/loss differences.

answers.answer: 1. “First Balance +£3 per Company region.” Then may repeatedly attempt Govern, paying £1 treasury per die, with no penalty. 2. “Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region, even on successful roll. On failure add another unrest to every Company region.” 3. On success, the Governor General's family takes £1 from the bank per Company region, then must choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China; place a regiment in any Army; or add £2 to Balance or any office treasury except its own, while adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must put their unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governor General: quoted starting revenue, check effects, success benefits and limit.

answers.answer: 1. Company and extra ships are exempt and never roll storm checks. Player-owned ships in Company fleets check in affected sea zones; China ships count as Eastern. Firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy, even though on a charter; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. 2. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue or sinks a ship already fatigued; 5–6 sinks. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard unfatigued.
answers.evidence: Events—Storm exposure table and roll procedure: quoted ship eligibility and results.

answers.answer: 1. “Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed.” 2. “If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades.” 3. “A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascades' effects.”
answers.evidence: Events—Closing orders and Cascades: full quoted destination and cascade rule.

answers.answer: 1. Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the region shown by the top stack tile; if all its orders are closed, it Cascades. 2. Windfall owners take £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. 3. Shuffle makes Elephant's March, then shuffles that tile with the remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place them on top. If the draw stack is empty, March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events table: Turmoil, Windfall and Shuffle rows: quoted event procedures and empty-stack exception.

answers.answer: 1. “Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier.” 2. Elephant Marches only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events table—Leader row: quoted sovereign/dominated effect and March condition.

answers.answer: 1. If Elephant is on a border, Peace opens orders connected across that border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. 2. If Elephant is wholly inside a region, Peace instead opens all its orders and removes its unrest. Then Elephant Marches.
answers.evidence: Events table—Peace row: quoted border and inside-region procedures.

answers.answer: 1. “Sovereign attacker's whole empire strength + event modifier must be greater than defender's whole empire strength.” Equal strength does not win; on failure the attacker loses one tower. 2. On success replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire or flags form.
answers.evidence: Events—Invasion Crisis: quoted strict comparison, failure, flag change and no-flags condition.

answers.answer: 1. Compare only the rebelling region's strength plus event modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other regions of the empire do not count. The attack must be strictly greater, so a tie does not win. 2. “Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.”
answers.evidence: Events—Rebellion Crisis: quoted included regions, strict comparison and failure result.

answers.answer: 1. On Region Loss, Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in the associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Return Governor office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies; remove Governor overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier, and region loses its Presidency association. 2. Invasion Crisis closes all its orders (or Cascades if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost so far this turn, including this one: first −1, second additional −2, etc. 3. “Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.”
answers.evidence: Events—Region Loss: quoted destinations, officer checks, loot/control status, order effects and Standing escalation.

answers.answer: 1. “After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region.” 2. On the chosen region, put Elephant fully inside a Company region; point it toward its sovereign in a dominated region; or point it across the tile's shape-marked border in a sovereign region. If that neighbor is already dominated by the actor, choose the first clockwise neighbor that is not. If all neighbors are dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape's border, pointing toward the empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events—Elephant's March: quoted destination and posture rules.

answers.answer: 1. Roll the storm die for target regions: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all-storms means each of them, and no storm indication means the top-stack region. For each target, roll an ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. 2. On success, close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target's flag and all matching flags if it is a capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. 3. The ordinary die is both attack strength and the basis for halved resulting towers; unrest does not add to primary strength or set tower level. The event still uses Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks.
answers.evidence: Events—Foreign Invasion row and FAQ ruling: quoted target procedure, effects and designer clarification.

answers.answer: 1. The PM must draw at least one law, revealing them one at a time. After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total; then choose any one revealed law and discard the others. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and ends drawing immediately. 2. Before voting, PM moves the dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping on the first policy space matching the selected law's bottom icon; that space fixes target and consequence. Read law and set Vote marker to its printed starting support.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: quoted draw limits, dilemma exception and policy selection procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Tax: each family pays £1 to the bank per target it owns; each unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Fitted ships of lost shipyards stay in play and that shipyard is unavailable until its ship returns; losing a prize/luxury removes its VP. 2. If selected policy includes windows, window tax additionally requires payment for each window on enterprises and each family member's prize; return enterprise/prize member if unable. 3. Bonus: the bank pays each family £1 per target it owns. 4. Power: swap target Power marker with the next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Policy table: quoted Tax, Window tax, Bonus and Power effects.

answers.answer: 1. Starting with PM and clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Each card's votes may be used only once in the entire vote across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until resolution, so it cannot vote again in a later round of that vote. 2. Adjust support up or down; tracks are unlimited. PM may call another full round or stop after each round. A round with no votes must end voting.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting: quoted cash/card vote costs, once-per-vote rule and round control.

answers.answer: 1. A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, they cannot vote for during this vote. Track all opposition votes: biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader; if tied, current holder retains it. 2. With recipient's consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose; add those votes to that person's opposition total. 3. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of the “Vote with my enterprises” promise.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting: quoted stance changes, Opposition Leader tiebreak, coalition consent and PM exception.

answers.answer: 1. Pay printed upkeep separately for each family member on a prize. If unpaid, return that member and lose the prize's printed VP; negotiating help remains possible while game continues. On the final turn, perform upkeep but skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. 2. On a nonfinal turn, return writers on orders to associated Presidency Writers boxes using dividers to preserve affiliation; return filled tokens and dividers to supply; return extra ships to supply; reactivate exhausted Army officers and regiments; exhaust active local alliances without reactivating them; fitted player ships keep fatigue and Trade itself never exhausts ships; advance one turn, then begin London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh: quoted prize payment rule, final-turn condition and every refresh table row.

answers.answer: 1. Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply, not Pensioners, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms where they own a share; the printed prize cost can exceed the marker when discounts cover the difference. No retirement from a firm whose marker is absent or zero. 2. Spouse discounts can allow a higher printed-cost prize; retirement otherwise follows normal rules, including prestige eligibility. 3. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success or failure, before normal final-scoring steps; no display cards in Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Special retirement: quoted limit, cash cap, marker restriction, discounts and Final Scoring timing.

answers.answer: 1. Firm London treasury receives the bank's £5 per investment; it pays ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses. Firm India treasury receives trade proceeds and pays dividends/expenses. 2. Investment money comes from the bank to London; family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries. 3. Fitting a ship from a shipyard costs £3 from the firm's London treasury to the bank. Trade bids are paid from London to the bank. Firm expenses may use either or both treasuries. Dividends come from India treasury only.
answers.evidence: Deregulation treasury description, Firms phase—Ships, firm trade checks, and Firm expenses/dividends: quoted cash destinations.

answers.answer: “After Family share creation, before Hiring, take investments actions without set order until nobody wishes more. Manager resolves timing conflicts within firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then choose strategies.”
answers.evidence: Firms phase—investments: complete phase timing and conflict resolution sentence.

answers.answer: 1. A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player's shipyard, but must have that shipyard owner's consent; pay £3 from the firm's London treasury to the bank. 2. A firm may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with that owner's consent: pay £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued into Shipping treasury. 3. “Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.”
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Ships: quoted ownership consent, cost/payment destinations, and prohibited ships.

answers.answer: “Only a player who manages NO firm at all may initiate [a hostile takeover]; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.”
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Hostile takeover: quoted eligibility, consent and transfer procedure.

answers.answer: 1. “Managers negotiate with every shareholder's consent.” Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied. 2. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. If the primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners' supplies, with those owners' consent. The entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer, and primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Merger: quoted consent, primary selection, asset/charter and ten-share rules.

answers.answer: 1. Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; it still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. 2. Hobnob firm ships are exempt from storms. 3. At Revenue, firms pay charter-ship costs plus the higher of share count or firm value; either or both treasuries may be used.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies—Hobnob row, firm storm rule, and expenses procedure: quoted effects.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules even when the ten-share cap prevents more shares. Use a Company share or workshop contribution; the normal restrictions still apply, including not using shares created this turn (even if traded away), not using the Chairman share, and not using Company shares when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. 2. Emergency investment pays expenses, loses any remaining cash, and lowers Value one space per emergency investment. At ten shares the contribution still contributes £5 to London but creates no share under the ordinary investment rule.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Invest and Firm expenses/rescue: quoted contribution restrictions, cap, and emergency investment effects.

answers.answer: “Alternatively make an emergency negotiated merger with only ONE other firm. The normal merger procedure still applies, including every involved shareholder's consent. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.”
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: quoted emergency merger procedure.

answers.answer: “All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm: shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.”
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Voluntary dissolution: quoted consent, destinations and workshop status.

answers.answer: 1. In Final Scoring, before ordinary Power/Court/final-outcome scoring, for each player separately add VP from all their shares across all their firms, then round that player's total down once. Deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. This firm scoring precedes ordinary scoring whether the Company survives or fails. 2. Per-share Value rates: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2. 3. Separately, ordinary Company shares add Court's current VP if Company survived, but subtract that value per share if Company failed; on failure add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order, firm-track VP rates, and Court/workshops: quoted timing, rounding, Debtor's Prison and survival effects.

answers.answer: Prize cost / upkeep / VP / windows per family member: £2 / £0 / 0 / 0; £4 / £1 / 2 / 1; £8 / £2 / 4 / 2; £14 / £3 / 8 / 3; £20 / £4 / 12 / 4.
answers.evidence: Prizes table: all five rows, columns cost, upkeep, VP, windows.

answers.answer: 1. 1710 runs turns 1–5; it has no deregulation procedures. 2. 1758 runs turns 3–7; it starts with a monopoly and deregulation can be voted in. 3. 1813 runs turns 5–8 and begins deregulated. 4. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8, has the same starting position as 1710, with deregulation available.
answers.evidence: Scenario scope and scenario figures table: quoted turn ranges and deregulation status.

answers.answer: 1. 1710: initial Standing £10 expectations / Debt 0; each office treasury £3; Royal Protection; one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 2. 1758: initial Standing £12 expectations / Debt 3; each office treasury £4; Calico Acts; one regiment per Army and one Company ship in East Indian. Put Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table: 1710 and 1758 rows; setup paragraph specifies Bengal control token.

answers.answer: 1. 1813 starts on turn 5 and ends on turn 8, with Standing £10 expectations / Debt 0; each office treasury £3; Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side) and Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. 2. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court; create China; place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies; return Governor General law to the box and put its office overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Copy the exact map components from the reverse of the scenario card.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table and 1813 setup paragraph: quoted initial setup and changes.

answers.answer: Most/second Power awards are 3/1 VP if final turn is 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, and 8/4 if turn 7–8. In a tie for first, each tied player gets only the lower award and there is no other award; players tied for second receive none.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Power award: quoted award ranges and tied-first/second rules.

answers.answer: 1. Initial Power positions: Social 2 power, Company shares 1, Shipping and Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations are £4/6/8/10/12/14/16, and reset S is above £10. 2. Lined Standing £4/6/8 or Debt 5/6/7/8 permits PM to call special Deregulation vote. Starred Standing £4 or Debt 8 requires PM to call it.
answers.evidence: Setup—Start Power positions and Deregulation thresholds: quoted values and permit/require distinction.

answers.answer: According to the designer ruling, unrest does not add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for both attack strength and halving to create towers. On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all target orders once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead. Region Loss does not close them a second time.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Foreign Invasion and unrest: quoted ruling and order closure correction.

answers.answer: 1. If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it means failure. 2. Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take from bank cash equal to that actual Balance reduction. 3. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and office card to vacancies. 4. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again.
answers.evidence: Applicable official errata: quoted four card corrections.

answers.answer: 1. Set Company Balance to £5, Power tokens on their indicated starting positions, family VP markers to zero, local alliances in their named Army boxes, and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. 2. Choose scenario and follow its setup card for Standing, Debt, office treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political map of India. Put Turn marker on its date and point PM dial arm to matching date; scenario card determines final turn.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2: quoted shared setup markers and scenario-specific setup instructions.

answers.answer: 1. The normal turn sequence is London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. 2. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at very start of turn before London Season. Firms phase follows Family and is included if deregulated. Skip London Season on the game's first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: quoted phase order and first-turn/special-vote timing.

answers.answer: 1. “Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize.” Pensioners need not all retire: unused pensioners do not remain for another turn. 2. For each retired pensioner, pay its printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay the bank.
answers.evidence: London Season—Retirements: quoted first player/order, optional retirement, destinations, VP and payment timing.

answers.answer: “Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag: it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.”
answers.evidence: India terminology: quoted last-dominated-region rule and cause-independence.
Scoring—Firm-track VP per share: complete value-to-VP table sentence.

answers.answer: 1. “Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action.” 2. “After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain.” If no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order.
answers.evidence: Family phase: quoted action order and New Company shares timing/procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Follow the red ribbon: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent, if created. 2. Skip each vacant office. Within each Presidency, President chooses order of Commander, Governors and Trade, and each position finishes before the next acts. Each office uses only its own treasury. A Governor General occupies Director of Trade's slot/turn position.
answers.evidence: Company Operation: quoted office order, vacancy rule and Presidency sequence; Governor General procedure says it uses former Director's turn position.

answers.answer: 1. “First roll the storm die”: its sea-zone result affects that zone, three storms affects all sea zones, and no storm indication means no storm checks. Resolve required storms before drawing any event. Company and extra ships are exempt; player-owned ships in Company fleets check in affected zones; China ships count Eastern; firm ships count in the zone on their firm strategy; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship. 2. The same storm die face specifies the number of India events. Then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack for as many events as printed on that face. Where an event uses a region, normally read the back of the new top tile, not the tile just drawn, subject to that event's location rule.
answers.evidence: Events in India opening paragraph and Storm exposure table: quoted phase order, ship eligibility and tile draw sequence.

answers.answer: 1. For an ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, tail is the attacker/acting region and head is defender. A sovereign actor, shown by a large capital flag or an unflagged dome, causes Invasion. A dominated actor, shown by a small flag or no dome, causes Rebellion against its sovereign. If Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. 2. Thus the map's flags and dome identify sovereignty/dominance: sovereign is dome without flag or capital/star flag; dominated is small flag or no dome. A capital/star flag identifies the empire's capital.
answers.evidence: India terminology and Events—ordinary Crisis classifier: quoted Elephant orientation and sovereign/dominated markers.
